{{short description|Egyptian chemist and alleged bomb maker}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Midhat Mursi al-Sayid Umar''' ({{langx|ar|مدحت مرسي السيد عمر}}), also known as '''Abu Khabab al-Masri''' ({{langx|ar|أبو خباب المصري}}; 29 April 1953 in [[Egypt]] – 28 July 2008 in [[Pakistan]]) was a chemist and alleged top bomb maker for [[al-Qaeda]] and part of [[Osama bin Laden]]'s inner circle. The United States had a $5 million bounty on his head. Although reported to have been killed in a U.S. attack in January 2006, he survived and intelligence officials believe he went on to attempt to resurrect al-Qaeda's program to develop or obtain [[weapons of mass destruction]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.latimes.com/news/printedition/front/la-fg-khabab3feb03,1,1148872.story?ctrack=5&cset=true|title=Al Qaeda said to focus on WMDs:A key operative and chemical engineer who was reported to have been slain is alive and leading the effort, officials say|work=Los Angeles Times|first=Josh|last=Meyer|date=3 February 2008}}</ref> On 28 July 2008, Mursi was killed in an American [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|drone]] attack in [[South Waziristan|South Waziristan, Pakistan]].<ref name="death_BBC">{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/7529419.stm|title=Al-Qaeda chemical expert 'killed'|publisher=BBC News|date=28 July 2008}}</ref>

==Al-Qaeda activities==
Umar is believed by U.S. authorities to have run the infamous [[Derunta training camp]] in [[Afghanistan]] where he is reported to have used [[dog]]s and other animals for his [[chemical]] [[experiment]]s.  He is also alleged to have written an explosives manual, and to have personally trained [[Richard Reid (terrorist)|Richard Reid]], the so-called "shoe bomber", as well as [[Zacarias Moussaoui]]. The manual is still in use by al-Qaeda operatives today.

==Wrong photo==
The [[CIA]] acknowledged on 26 January 2006 that they had been using a photo of [[Abu Hamza al-Masri]] in their wanted photo for Midhat Mursi, who shared the similar alias '''"Abu Khabab al Masri"'''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071031100609/http://www.upi.com/NewsTrack/Top_News/2006/01/26/report_us_used_wrong_terrorist_photo/5209/], ''[[United Press International]]'', 26 January 2006</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070312093904/http://www.nbc4.tv/news/6468397/detail.html], ''[[NBC]]'', 26 January 2006</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20161220072012/http://www.nbcnews.com/id/11042211/ U.S. posts wrong photo of ‘al-Qaida operative’: After year and a half, wrong man's photo removed from wanted page], ''[[NBC News]]'', 26 January 2006</ref> Mursi's poster at the [[Rewards for Justice Program]] was changed to a different photo.

==Misreported death==
He was reported to have been killed in the [[Damadola airstrike]] in [[Pakistan]] on 13 January 2006 along with several other al-Qaeda operatives.<ref>[http://www.rewardsforjustice.net/english/wanted_captured/index.cfm?page=midhat_mursi WANTED: Midhat Mursi al-Sayid 'Umar – Up to $5 Million Reward] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060110180819/http://www.rewardsforjustice.net/english/wanted_captured/index.cfm?page=Midhat_Mursi |date=10 January 2006 }}. [[Rewards for Justice Program]], US Department of State</ref><ref>[https://abcnews.go.com/WNT/Investigation/story?id=1517986 U.S. Strike Killed Al Qaeda Bomb Maker: Terror Big Also Trained 'Shoe Bomber,' Moussaoui], ''[[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]]'', 18 January 2006</ref> The target of the strike was [[Ayman al-Zawahiri]], al-Qaeda's then-number 2 man. Pakistani intelligence originally confirmed Mursi's death in the airstrike along with al-Zawahiri's alleged son-in-law, Abdul Rehman al-Maghribi, but on 8 September 2007, the ''Washington Post'', citing "U.S. and Pakistani officials", said that all the dead in that raid had been locals.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/09/08/AR2007090801845_2.html The New Al-Qaeda Central], ''[[Washington Post]]'', 8 September 2007</ref>

==Death==
On 28 July 2008, [[the Pentagon]] confirmed al-Masri was killed in a missile strike in [[Pakistan]] that also killed five other militants including Ibrahim, the son of [[Ahmad Salama Mabruk]].<ref name="death_BBC" /><ref>[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]], [http://thenational.ae/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080824/OPINION/95365605/1126&template=opinion&template=tipafriend&template=tipafriend&template=tipafriend Zawahiri lauds chemical expert] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140506095318/http://www.thenational.ae/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20080824%2FOPINION%2F95365605%2F1126&template=opinion&template=tipafriend&template=tipafriend&template=tipafriend |date=6 May 2014 }}, 24 August 2008</ref><ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/world/feedarticle/7698321 Al-Qaida: Explosives expert wanted by US killed]</ref>

==Family==
Mursi's son, Mohammed al-Masri, was born in 1980 in [[Aqaba]], [[Jordan]]. He has been associated with the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] as well as al-Qaeda, though he has expressed dissatisfaction with the conduct of the former.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mekhennet |first1=Souad |authorlink1=Souad Mekhennet |last2=Miller |first2=Greg |date=5 August 2016 |title=Bloodline: He's the son of Osama bin Laden's bombmaker. Then ISIS wanted him as one of their own. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/national/wp/2016/08/05/2016/08/05/bombmaker/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=5 August 2016}}</ref>
